source.text: אֲנִ֤י הַגֶּ֨בֶר֙ רָאָ֣ה עֳנִ֔י בְּשֵׁ֖בֶט עֶבְרָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: I [am] the man [who] has seen affliction by [the] rod of his fury.

en.L: I [am] the man [who] has seen affliction \q under the rod of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fury.
en.B: I am the man who has lived through affliction \q beneath the rod of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger.
en.R: I am the man who has suffered so much, \q struck by the rod of God's anger.

pt.L: Eu [sou] o homem [que] viu a aflição \q sob a vara do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} furor.
pt.B: Eu sou o homem que passou pela aflição \q debaixo da vara da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira.
pt.R: Eu sou o homem que sofreu tanto, \q ferido pela vara da ira de Deus.

fr.L: Je [suis] l’homme [qui] a vu l’affliction \q sous la verge de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fureur.
fr.B: Je suis l’homme qui a connu l’affliction \q sous le bâton de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère.
fr.R: Je suis l’homme qui a tant souffert, \q frappé par le bâton de la colère de Dieu.

es.L: Yo [soy] el hombre [que] ha visto la aflicción \q bajo la vara de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} furor.
es.B: Yo soy el hombre que ha pasado por la aflicción \q bajo la vara de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} furor.
es.R: Yo soy el hombre que ha sufrido tanto, \q golpeado por la vara del enojo de Dios.

vi.L: Tôi [là] người đã thấy khốn khổ \q dưới roi thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Tôi là người đã từng trải qua khốn khổ \q dưới ngọn roi cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Tôi là người đã chịu khổ quá nhiều, \q bị đánh bằng roi của cơn giận Đức Chúa Trời.

sw.L: Mimi [ndimi] mtu aliyeona mateso \q chini ya fimbo ya hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kali.
sw.B: Mimi ni mtu aliyepitia mateso \q chini ya fimbo ya hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Mimi ni mtu aliyeteseka sana, \q nikipigwa kwa fimbo ya hasira ya Mungu.

ko.L: 나는 고난을 본 사람이다, \q 그분의 격노의 막대기 아래에서.
ko.B: 나는 그분의 진노의 막대기 아래에서 \q 고난을 겪어 온 사람이다.
ko.R: 나는 하나님의 분노의 막대기에 맞아 \q 큰 고통을 겪은 사람이다.

decisions.choice: an alphabet poem: three verses for each letter
decisions.reason: Like chapters 1, 2 and 4, this chapter is an acrostic, but here each of the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet begins three verses in a row, so the chapter has sixty-six verses: verses 1-3 begin with aleph, 4-6 with beth, and so on to taw in 64-66. As in chapters 2 and 4, pe comes before ayin (verses 46-51; see the note at 2:1). The lines keep the lament rhythm described at 1:1, a longer half followed by a shorter one.

decisions.choice: the man: one who speaks for the suffering city, never named
decisions.reason: The speaker is a man (geber, a word for a grown, strong man, used again in verses 27, 35 and 39) who tells of his own suffering. He is not named. Some have heard Jeremiah, whose life fits much of it: he was beaten, put in stocks and let down into a cistern (Jeremiah 20:2; 38:6; compare verses 53-55). Others hear Zion, the city of chapters 1-2, now speaking as a man; others an everyman, any faithful person of Judah, whose story becomes the people's ('we', verses 40-47). The text does not settle it, and the man's voice moves into the community's and back again.

decisions.choice: his: God, not yet named
decisions.reason: The poem says 'he' and 'his' for the one who strikes the man without naming him until verse 18, where it is the LORD. The rod is a father's or ruler's rod of punishment (2 Samuel 7:14; Isaiah 10:5).

decisions.choice: a new voice, with no marks of quotation
decisions.reason: After the poet and Zion in chapters 1-2, a man now speaks in the first person. As with Zion's words, his poem is not set off as a quotation.

decisions.choice: struck by the rod of God's anger
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the Hebrew leaves as 'his' (m3), and says the rod struck him.

decisions.choice: "l’homme", with masculine agreement in chapter 3 ("je suis devenu", "il m’a enfermé")
decisions.reason: A new voice speaks here (m4): a man (gever), not Zion, so French agreement turns masculine until the people speak as "nous" (verses 40–47); his words take no quotation marks, as the English.

decisions.choice: "el hombre", with masculine agreement through the chapter
decisions.reason: The speaker of this chapter is a man (geber), not Zion, so his words agree in the masculine (desolado, devastado, solo). As in chapters 1 and 2, his voice takes no quotation marks; only words he reports (verses 18, 24, 54, 56, 57) take « ».

decisions.choice: The triple alphabetic order (three verses to each letter) is not reproduced; the lines follow the sense
alternatives: Imitating the pattern with the Vietnamese alphabet
decisions.reason: As in 1:1: Vietnamese cannot keep the letter order without forcing the sense; the meaning decisions name each letter.

decisions.choice: "người" for the man (geber), who speaks as "tôi" and calls God "Ngài" through the chapter
decisions.reason: The man speaks for the suffering city and is never named; "người" is plain and is repeated for the same word in 3:27 and 3:35, so the link can be heard. He says "tôi" even to God, as Zion does in chapters 1–2.

decisions.choice: "mtu" for geber (the man)
decisions.reason: Geber is a man as a grown, strong person. "Mwanamume" would put the stress on his being male, which is not the point of the poem; "mtu" keeps him an unnamed sufferer who speaks for his people. The same word is used for geber in verses 27, 35 and 39.

decisions.choice: the man speaks about God in the plain style with -시- ("그분께서 ... 하셨다"); "사람" for geber
decisions.reason: The man of chapter 3 tells his story to the reader, so he speaks in the plain written style and gives God the honorific, as Korean narration does. He turns to God in 합쇼체 only where the Hebrew does: the plea of 3:19, the confession of 3:23, and from 3:42 to the end. "사람" is neutral and also serves for the same word in 3:27 and 3:35, 39.

records.literal_gloss: Me he has driven and made walk [in] darkness and not light.

en.L: He has driven me and made [me] walk \q [in] darkness and not [in] light.
en.B: He has led me away and made me walk \q in darkness, not in light.
en.R: He has driven me on like an animal \q into darkness where there is no light.

pt.L: Ele me conduziu e [me] fez andar \q [nas] trevas e não [na] luz.
pt.B: Ele me levou para longe e me fez andar \q nas trevas, não na luz.
pt.R: Ele me empurrou como se empurra um animal \q para a escuridão, onde não há luz.

fr.L: Il m’a conduit et fait marcher \q [dans] les ténèbres et non [dans] la lumière.
fr.B: Il m’a emmené et m’a fait marcher \q dans les ténèbres, et non dans la lumière.
fr.R: Il m’a poussé devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} comme une bête \q dans une obscurité où il n’y a aucune lumière.

es.L: Me ha conducido y me ha hecho andar \q [en] tinieblas y no [en] luz.
es.B: Me ha llevado lejos y me ha hecho caminar \q en oscuridad, no en luz.
es.R: Me ha arreado como a un animal \q hacia la oscuridad, donde no hay luz.

vi.L: Ngài đã dẫn tôi đi và bắt [tôi] bước \q [trong] bóng tối chứ không [trong] ánh sáng.
vi.B: Ngài đã dẫn tôi đi và bắt tôi bước \q trong bóng tối, không phải trong ánh sáng.
vi.R: Ngài đã lùa tôi đi như lùa súc vật \q vào bóng tối, nơi không có ánh sáng.

sw.L: Ameniongoza na kunitembeza \q [katika] giza wala si [katika] nuru.
sw.B: Ameniongoza mbali na kunitembeza \q gizani, si katika nuru.
sw.R: Amenifukuza kama mnyama \q hadi gizani ambako hakuna nuru.

ko.L: 그분께서 나를 몰아 \q 빛이 아닌 어둠 [속을] 걷게 하셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 나를 이끌어 내셔서 \q 빛이 없는 어둠 속을 걷게 하셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 나를 짐승처럼 몰아 \q 빛이 하나도 없는 어둠 속으로 가게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: driven: led or herded along, as a shepherd drives a flock
decisions.reason: The verb (nahag) is used for driving animals or leading a flock (Genesis 31:18; Psalm 80:2). The one who should lead his people to safety drives this man the wrong way.

decisions.choice: darkness and not light: trouble with no relief
decisions.reason: Darkness stands for distress and the absence of God's help; light is rescue and favor (Amos 5:18-20; Isaiah 59:9).

decisions.choice: like an animal
decisions.reason: Readable makes the herding picture of the verb plain (m1).

source.text: אַ֣ךְ בִּ֥י יָשֻׁ֛ב יַהֲפֹ֥ךְ יָד֖וֹ כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Surely against me he turns again, he turns his hand all the day.

en.L: Surely against me {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turns again and again {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand \q all the day.
en.B: Yes, it is me {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} strikes with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q time after time, all day long.
en.R: He keeps striking me with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q over and over, all day long.

pt.L: Certamente contra mim {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} volta e torna a voltar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão \q o dia todo.
pt.B: Sim, é a mim que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} golpeia com a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão, \q vez após vez, o dia inteiro.
pt.R: Ele continua me batendo com a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão, \q de novo e de novo, o dia inteiro.

fr.L: Oui, contre moi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} retourne encore et encore {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main \q tout le jour.
fr.B: Oui, c’est moi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} frappe de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main, \q encore et encore, toute la journée.
fr.R: Il ne cesse de me frapper de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main, \q encore et encore, toute la journée.

es.L: Ciertamente contra mí vuelve y vuelve {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano \q todo el día.
es.B: Sí, es a mí a quien golpea con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano, \q una y otra vez, todo el día.
es.R: No deja de golpearme con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano, \q una y otra vez, todo el día.

vi.L: Thật vậy, nghịch cùng tôi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trở tay của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hết lần này đến lần khác \q suốt cả ngày.
vi.B: Phải, chính tôi là kẻ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đánh bằng tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q hết lần này đến lần khác, suốt ngày.
vi.R: Ngài cứ đánh tôi bằng tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q lần này đến lần khác, suốt cả ngày.

sw.L: Hakika juu yangu anaugeuza mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} tena na tena \q mchana kutwa.
sw.B: Naam, ni mimi anayenipiga kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, \q tena na tena, mchana kutwa.
sw.R: Ananipiga kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} bila kukoma, \q tena na tena, siku nzima.

ko.L: 정녕 그분께서 나를 향해 그분의 손을 거듭거듭 돌리신다, \q 온종일.
ko.B: 그렇다. 그분께서 손을 들어 나를 치시고 \q 하루 종일 치고 또 치신다.
ko.R: 그분께서 손으로 나를 계속 치신다. \q 몇 번이고, 온종일 치신다.

decisions.choice: turns again, turns: he strikes again and again
decisions.reason: Two verbs stand side by side, 'he returns' and 'he turns'; the first makes the second repeated. The hand is turned against the man over and over.

decisions.choice: his hand: his power to strike
decisions.reason: God's hand turned against someone means his power used against them in judgment (Isaiah 1:25; Psalm 81:15).

decisions.choice: surely: an emphatic word
decisions.reason: The small word ('akh) stresses what follows: it is against me, and no one else, that he turns. It can also mean 'only'.

decisions.choice: keeps striking me with his hand
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what turning the hand against someone means (m2).

records.literal_gloss: He has worn out my flesh and my skin; he has broken my bones.

en.L: He has worn away my flesh and my skin; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has broken my bones.
en.B: He has worn out my flesh and skin \q and shattered my bones.
en.R: He has made my body waste away. \q He has broken my bones.

pt.L: Ele desgastou a minha carne e a minha pele; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quebrou os meus ossos.
pt.B: Ele gastou a minha carne e a minha pele \q e despedaçou os meus ossos.
pt.R: Ele fez o meu corpo definhar. \q Ele quebrou os meus ossos.

fr.L: Il a usé ma chair et ma peau ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a brisé mes os.
fr.B: Il a usé ma chair et ma peau \q et fracassé mes os.
fr.R: Il a fait dépérir mon corps. \q Il a brisé mes os.

es.L: Ha desgastado mi carne y mi piel; \q ha quebrado mis huesos.
es.B: Ha consumido mi carne y mi piel \q y ha hecho pedazos mis huesos.
es.R: Ha hecho que mi cuerpo se consuma. \q Me ha roto los huesos.

vi.L: Ngài đã làm hao mòn thịt và da tôi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã bẻ gãy xương cốt tôi.
vi.B: Ngài đã làm thịt da tôi hao mòn \q và đập nát xương cốt tôi.
vi.R: Ngài đã làm thân thể tôi tiều tụy. \q Ngài đã bẻ gãy xương cốt tôi.

sw.L: Ameichakaza nyama yangu na ngozi yangu; \q ameivunja mifupa yangu.
sw.B: Ameudhoofisha mwili wangu na ngozi yangu \q na kuipondaponda mifupa yangu.
sw.R: Ameufanya mwili wangu udhoofike. \q Ameivunja mifupa yangu.

ko.L: 그분께서 내 살과 내 가죽을 닳게 하시고, \q 내 뼈들을 꺾으셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 내 살과 살갗을 쇠하게 하시고 \q 내 뼈들을 부수셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 내 몸을 야위게 하셨다. \q 내 뼈들을 부러뜨리셨다.

decisions.choice: second letter: beth (verses 4-6)
decisions.reason: Verses 4-6 each begin with beth, the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: worn out: made to waste away, like an old garment
decisions.reason: The verb (balah) is used of clothes that wear out (Deuteronomy 8:4). The man's body is wasting away under his suffering, as in Job 13:28 and Psalm 32:3.

decisions.choice: broken my bones: crushed him through and through
decisions.reason: Bones are the frame of a person's strength. Broken bones picture complete collapse (Psalm 51:10; Isaiah 38:13, where the LORD breaks bones 'like a lion').

decisions.choice: my body
decisions.reason: Readable says 'body' for 'flesh and skin'.

records.literal_gloss: He has built against me and surrounded [me with] poison and hardship.

en.L: He has built against me and encircled [me] \q [with] poison and hardship.
en.B: He has built siege walls against me \q and closed me in with bitter poison and hardship.
en.R: He has attacked me as an army attacks a city. \q He has surrounded me with bitter suffering and trouble.

pt.L: Ele construiu contra mim e [me] cercou \q [de] veneno e de sofrimento.
pt.B: Ele levantou muralhas de cerco contra mim \q e me fechou com veneno amargo e sofrimento.
pt.R: Ele me atacou como um exército ataca uma cidade. \q Ele me cercou de sofrimento amargo e de aflição.

fr.L: Il a bâti contre moi et [m’]a entouré \q [de] poison et de peine.
fr.B: Il a dressé contre moi des murs de siège \q et m’a enfermé dans un poison amer et dans la peine.
fr.R: Il m’a attaqué comme une armée attaque une ville. \q Il m’a entouré de souffrances amères et de malheurs.

es.L: Ha edificado contra mí y [me] ha rodeado \q [de] veneno y fatiga.
es.B: Ha levantado muros de asedio contra mí \q y me ha encerrado con veneno amargo y penalidades.
es.R: Me ha atacado como un ejército ataca una ciudad. \q Me ha rodeado de sufrimiento amargo y de problemas.

vi.L: Ngài đã xây nghịch cùng tôi và vây quanh [tôi] \q [bằng] chất độc và gian nan.
vi.B: Ngài đã đắp lũy bao vây tôi \q và nhốt tôi trong chất độc đắng cay và gian khổ.
vi.R: Ngài đã tấn công tôi như một đạo quân tấn công một thành. \q Ngài đã vây tôi bằng nỗi đau đắng cay và khốn khó.

sw.L: Amejenga dhidi yangu na kunizunguka \q [kwa] sumu na taabu.
sw.B: Amejenga kuta za kuzingira dhidi yangu \q na kunizingira kwa sumu chungu na taabu.
sw.R: Amenishambulia kama jeshi linavyoshambulia mji. \q Amenizunguka kwa mateso machungu na taabu.

ko.L: 그분께서 나를 대적하여 쌓으시고 \q 독과 고난으로 [나를] 에워싸셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 나를 치시려고 포위 벽을 쌓으시고, \q 쓰디쓴 독과 고난으로 나를 에워싸셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 군대가 성을 공격하듯 나를 공격하셨다. \q 쓰라린 고통과 괴로움으로 나를 에워싸셨다.

decisions.choice: built against me and surrounded: the picture of a siege
decisions.reason: To 'build against' a city is to raise siege works around it, and to surround it is to cut it off (Ezekiel 4:2; 2 Kings 25:1). The man is besieged as Jerusalem was.

decisions.choice: poison and hardship: bitter suffering
decisions.reason: The first word (rosh) names a bitter, poisonous plant (Deuteronomy 29:17; Jeremiah 8:14); here it is the bitterness of suffering. The second (tela'ah) is weariness and hardship (Exodus 18:8). The besieger's walls are made of misery.

decisions.choice: siege walls; bitter poison
decisions.reason: Balanced names what is built, and makes plain that the poison is the bitter kind (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: as an army attacks a city; bitter suffering
decisions.reason: Readable explains the siege picture and says what the poison stands for.

records.literal_gloss: In dark places he has made me dwell, like [the] dead of long ago.

en.L: In dark places {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made me dwell, \q like the dead of long ago.
en.B: He has made me live in dark places \q like those who died long ago.
en.R: He has made me live in darkness, \q like people who have been dead a long time.

pt.L: Em lugares escuros {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me fez habitar, \q como os mortos de há muito tempo.
pt.B: Ele me fez morar em lugares escuros \q como os que morreram há muito tempo.
pt.R: Ele me fez viver na escuridão, \q como as pessoas que estão mortas há muito tempo.

fr.L: Il m’a fait habiter dans des lieux obscurs, \q comme les morts d’autrefois.
fr.B: Il m’a fait vivre dans les ténèbres, \q comme ceux qui sont morts depuis longtemps.
fr.R: Il m’a fait vivre dans le noir, \q comme des gens morts depuis longtemps.

es.L: En lugares oscuros me ha hecho habitar, \q como los muertos de hace mucho.
es.B: Me ha hecho vivir en lugares oscuros, \q como los que murieron hace mucho tiempo.
es.R: Me ha hecho vivir en la oscuridad, \q como la gente que lleva mucho tiempo muerta.

vi.L: Trong những nơi tối tăm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã bắt tôi ở, \q như những người chết từ xưa.
vi.B: Ngài bắt tôi phải sống trong những nơi tối tăm \q như những người đã chết từ lâu đời.
vi.R: Ngài đã bắt tôi sống trong bóng tối, \q như những người đã chết từ lâu lắm rồi.

sw.L: Katika mahali pa giza amenikalisha, \q kama wafu wa zamani za kale.
sw.B: Amenifanya niishi mahali pa giza \q kama watu waliokufa zamani.
sw.R: Amenifanya niishi gizani, \q kama watu waliokufa siku nyingi.

ko.L: 그분께서 나를 어두운 곳에 살게 하셨다, \q 오래전에 죽은 자들처럼.
ko.B: 그분께서 나를 어두운 곳에서 살게 하셨다, \q 오래전에 죽은 사람들처럼.
ko.R: 그분께서 나를 어둠 속에서 살게 하셨다. \q 죽은 지 오래된 사람들처럼 살게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: the same words as Psalm 143:3
decisions.reason: The line is almost word for word the complaint of Psalm 143:3, where the enemy makes the psalmist sit in darkness 'like the dead of long ago'. The dark places are the grave or the world of the dead (Psalm 88:7).

decisions.choice: of long ago: dead for ages, long forgotten
decisions.reason: The word ('olam) here looks back a long time. He is like those who died long ago, forgotten and beyond help.

decisions.choice: me fez habitar em lugares escuros ... os mortos de há muito tempo
decisions.reason: The line is nearly the words of Psalm 143:3 (m1), so Literal keeps the Portuguese of that psalm's Literal, "fez-me habitar em lugares escuros como os mortos de há muito tempo", in Lamentations' own word order.

decisions.choice: the wording of the published French Psalm 143:3 at each level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is the same as Psalm 143:3 (m1), so French reuses that verse’s words at each level, changing only the tense at Readable.

decisions.choice: "me ha hecho habitar ... como los muertos de hace mucho"
decisions.reason: The line repeats Psalm 143:3 word for word in Hebrew, so Literal uses the wording of the Spanish Psalm 143:3 Literal.

decisions.choice: The wording of the published Psalm 143:3 ("những nơi tối tăm như những người chết từ xưa" / "đã chết từ lâu đời")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words are the same as in Psalm 143:3, so Literal and Balanced use that verse's Vietnamese and the echo can be heard.

source.text: גָּדַ֧ר בַּעֲדִ֛י וְלֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א הִכְבִּ֥יד נְחָשְׁתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: He has walled around me and not I will go out; he has made heavy my bronze.

en.L: He has walled me in, and I cannot go out; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made my bronze [chains] heavy.
en.B: He has hemmed me in, and I cannot get out; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has weighed me down with chains.
en.R: He has built a wall around me, and I cannot get out. \q He has put heavy chains on me.

pt.L: Ele me cercou com muro, e não posso sair; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tornou pesadas as minhas [correntes de] bronze.
pt.B: Ele me cercou, e não consigo sair; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me prendeu com correntes pesadas.
pt.R: Ele construiu um muro ao meu redor, e eu não consigo sair. \q Ele me pôs correntes pesadas.

fr.L: Il a muré autour de moi, et je ne peux pas sortir ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a alourdi mes [chaînes de] bronze.
fr.B: Il m’a enfermé, et je ne peux pas sortir ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a chargé de lourdes chaînes.
fr.R: Il a construit un mur autour de moi, et je ne peux pas sortir. \q Il m’a mis de lourdes chaînes.

es.L: Me ha cercado con muro, y no puedo salir; \q ha hecho pesadas mis [cadenas de] bronce.
es.B: Me ha encerrado, y no puedo salir; \q me ha agobiado con cadenas.
es.R: Ha construido un muro a mi alrededor, y no puedo salir. \q Me ha puesto cadenas pesadas.

vi.L: Ngài đã xây tường bao quanh tôi, và tôi không thể ra; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cho [xiềng] đồng của tôi nặng thêm.
vi.B: Ngài đã rào vây tôi, và tôi không thể thoát ra; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đè nặng tôi bằng xiềng xích.
vi.R: Ngài đã xây tường chung quanh tôi, và tôi không thể ra ngoài. \q Ngài đã đặt xiềng xích nặng nề trên tôi.

sw.L: Amenizungushia ukuta, wala siwezi kutoka; \q ameifanya mizito [minyororo yangu ya] shaba.
sw.B: Amenizingira, wala siwezi kutoka; \q amenilemea kwa minyororo.
sw.R: Amejenga ukuta kunizunguka, wala siwezi kutoka. \q Amenifunga minyororo mizito.

ko.L: 그분께서 나를 둘러 담을 쌓으시니 내가 나갈 수 없다. \q 그분께서 내 놋[사슬]을 무겁게 하셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 나를 가두셔서 빠져나갈 수 없게 하시고, \q 무거운 사슬로 나를 짓누르셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 내 주위에 담을 쌓으셔서 나는 나갈 수 없다. \q 그분께서 나에게 무거운 사슬을 채우셨다.

decisions.choice: third letter: gimel (verses 7-9)
decisions.reason: Verses 7-9 each begin with gimel, the third letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: my bronze: my bronze fetters
decisions.reason: 'Bronze' here means chains or fetters made of bronze, as in Judges 16:21 and 2 Kings 25:7, where Zedekiah was bound 'with bronze'.

decisions.choice: walled me in: shut him up with no way out
decisions.reason: The verb (gadar) is building a stone wall or hedge, as around a field. Job uses the picture for God blocking his way (Job 19:8; compare Hosea 2:8).

decisions.choice: chains
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the bronze was (m2).

source.text: גַּ֣ם כִּ֤י אֶזְעַק֙ וַאֲשַׁוֵּ֔עַ שָׂתַ֖ם תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Also when I cry out and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.

en.L: Even when I cry out and call for help, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stops up my prayer.
en.B: Even when I shout and plead for help, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps my prayer out.
en.R: I cry out and call for help, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} closes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ears to my prayer.

pt.L: Mesmo quando clamo e peço socorro, \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} bloqueia a minha oração.
pt.B: Mesmo quando grito e suplico por socorro, \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} barra a minha oração.
pt.R: Eu clamo e peço socorro, \q mas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fecha os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} ouvidos à minha oração.

fr.L: Même quand je crie et appelle au secours, \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ferme [l’accès à] ma prière.
fr.B: Même quand je crie et que j’appelle à l’aide, \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ferme la porte à ma prière.
fr.R: Je crie et j’appelle au secours, \q mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} bouche les oreilles devant ma prière.

es.L: Aun cuando clamo y pido auxilio, \q cierra el paso a mi oración.
es.B: Aunque grito y suplico ayuda, \q no deja entrar mi oración.
es.R: Clamo y pido ayuda, \q pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se tapa los oídos ante mi oración.

vi.L: Dù khi tôi kêu la và cầu cứu, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chặn lời cầu nguyện của tôi lại.
vi.B: Dù khi tôi kêu la và nài xin cứu giúp, \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vẫn gạt lời cầu nguyện của tôi ra ngoài.
vi.R: Tôi kêu la và xin cứu giúp, \q nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bịt tai trước lời cầu nguyện của tôi.

sw.L: Hata ninapolia na kuomba msaada, \q anayazuia maombi yangu.
sw.B: Hata ninapopiga kelele na kusihi msaada, \q anayafungia nje maombi yangu.
sw.R: Ninalia na kuomba msaada, \q lakini anaziba masikio {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} asisikie maombi yangu.

ko.L: 내가 부르짖고 도움을 청할 때에도 \q 그분께서 내 기도를 막으신다.
ko.B: 내가 소리치며 도와 달라고 애원해도 \q 그분께서 내 기도를 물리치신다.
ko.R: 내가 소리쳐 도움을 구하지만 \q 그분께서는 내 기도에 귀를 막으신다.

decisions.choice: shuts out: stops up, closes off
decisions.reason: The verb (satam, spelled here with a different first letter from usual) means to stop up or block, as wells are stopped up (Genesis 26:15). The man's prayer finds the way closed (compare verse 44).

decisions.choice: even when: the shutting out comes in spite of his crying
decisions.reason: 'Also' with 'when' adds this to the list of his troubles: even prayer does not get through.

decisions.choice: closes his ears to
decisions.reason: Readable gives a familiar picture for the verb 'stops up'.

records.literal_gloss: He has walled up my ways with hewn stone; my paths he has made crooked.

en.L: He has walled up my ways with cut stone; \q my paths {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made crooked.
en.B: He has walled off my road with cut stone; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made my paths twist.
en.R: He has built a stone wall across my road. \q He has made my paths twist and turn.

pt.L: Ele fechou com muro os meus caminhos com pedra lavrada; \q as minhas veredas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} entortou.
pt.B: Ele bloqueou o meu caminho com pedras lavradas; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fez as minhas veredas darem voltas.
pt.R: Ele construiu um muro de pedra no meio do meu caminho. \q Ele fez os meus caminhos darem voltas e mais voltas.

fr.L: Il a muré mes chemins de pierres taillées ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rendu tortueux mes sentiers.
fr.B: Il a barré ma route de pierres taillées ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rendu mes sentiers tortueux.
fr.R: Il a construit un mur de pierre en travers de ma route. \q Il a fait tourner et zigzaguer mes chemins.

es.L: Ha tapiado mis caminos con piedra labrada; \q mis senderos ha torcido.
es.B: Ha cerrado mi camino con piedra labrada; \q ha hecho que mis senderos se tuerzan.
es.R: Ha levantado un muro de piedra en medio de mi camino. \q Ha hecho que mis senderos den vueltas y más vueltas.

vi.L: Ngài đã lấy đá đẽo xây chắn các đường lối tôi; \q các nẻo đường tôi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cong queo.
vi.B: Ngài đã lấy đá đẽo xây tường chắn đường tôi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm các lối tôi đi quanh co.
vi.R: Ngài đã xây một bức tường đá chắn ngang đường tôi. \q Ngài đã làm các lối tôi đi quanh co, khúc khuỷu.

sw.L: Amezizingira njia zangu kwa mawe yaliyochongwa; \q mapito yangu ameyapotosha.
sw.B: Amezifunga njia zangu kwa ukuta wa mawe yaliyochongwa; \q ameyafanya mapito yangu yapindepinde.
sw.R: Amejenga ukuta wa mawe katikati ya njia yangu. \q Ameyafanya mapito yangu yapindepinde.

ko.L: 그분께서 다듬은 돌로 내 길들을 막으시고, \q 내 오솔길들을 굽게 하셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 다듬은 돌로 내 길을 가로막으시고, \q 내 길을 구불구불하게 만드셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 내 길에 돌담을 쌓아 막으셨다. \q 내 길을 이리저리 구부러지게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: cut stone: dressed stone, the strongest kind of wall
decisions.reason: The word (gazit) is stone cut and shaped for building (1 Kings 5:31; Isaiah 9:9). A wall of it cannot be pushed through.

decisions.choice: made my paths crooked: left him no straight way
decisions.reason: A crooked path leads nowhere and is hard to walk (Isaiah 59:8). Every way he tries ends in a dead end. The verb 'walled' repeats from verse 7.

source.text: דֹּ֣ב אֹרֵ֥ב הוּא֙ לִ֔י אֲרִ֖י בְּמִסְתָּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: A bear lying in wait he [is] to me, a lion in hiding places.

en.L: A bear lying in wait [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} to me, \q a lion in hiding places.
en.B: To me {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is like a bear waiting in ambush, \q like a lion crouching in hiding.
en.R: He waits to attack me like a bear, \q like a lion hiding in the bushes.

pt.L: Um urso à espreita {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} [é] para mim, \q um leão em esconderijos.
pt.B: Para mim {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é como um urso de tocaia, \q como um leão agachado no seu esconderijo.
pt.R: Ele espera para me atacar como um urso, \q como um leão escondido no mato.

fr.L: Il est pour moi un ours aux aguets, \q un lion dans des cachettes.
fr.B: Pour moi, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est comme un ours qui guette, \q comme un lion tapi dans sa cachette.
fr.R: Il attend pour m’attaquer, comme un ours, \q comme un lion caché dans les buissons.

es.L: Oso que acecha [es] {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para mí, \q león en escondrijos.
es.B: Para mí {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es como un oso al acecho, \q como un león agazapado en su escondite.
es.R: Espera para atacarme como un oso, \q como un león escondido entre los arbustos.

vi.L: Một con gấu rình rập [là] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đối với tôi, \q một con sư tử trong nơi ẩn nấp.
vi.B: Đối với tôi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như con gấu nằm rình, \q như con sư tử núp trong chỗ kín.
vi.R: Ngài rình để tấn công tôi như một con gấu, \q như một con sư tử nấp trong bụi rậm.

sw.L: Dubu anayeotea [ni] {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kwangu, \q simba mahali pa kujificha.
sw.B: Kwangu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni kama dubu anayevizia, \q kama simba aliyejificha.
sw.R: Ananivizia kama dubu, \q kama simba aliyejificha vichakani.

ko.L: 그분께서는 나에게 엎드려 기다리는 곰이시요, \q 숨은 곳에 있는 사자이시다.
ko.B: 그분께서는 나에게 숨어서 노리는 곰과 같으시고, \q 몸을 웅크리고 숨은 사자와 같으시다.
ko.R: 그분께서는 곰처럼 나를 덮치려고 기다리신다. \q 덤불 속에 숨은 사자처럼 기다리신다.

decisions.choice: fourth letter: daleth (verses 10-12)
decisions.reason: Verses 10-12 each begin with daleth, the fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: a bear ... a lion: God pictured as a beast of prey
decisions.reason: The man's suffering is so fierce that God seems to him like a predator. Hosea uses the same pictures for God's judgment on his people (Hosea 13:7-8), and Amos the bear and the lion together (Amos 5:19). It is how the man experiences God, not a full account of him; verses 22-33 say more.

decisions.choice: lion: the written and the read forms differ only in spelling
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell the longer form of the word for lion ('aryeh); the reading marked in the margin is the shorter form ('ari). Both mean 'lion'.

decisions.choice: hiding in the bushes
decisions.reason: Readable says where a lion hides; the Hebrew says 'in hiding places'.

records.literal_gloss: My ways he has turned aside and torn me in pieces; he has made me desolate.

en.L: My ways {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has turned aside, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has torn me apart; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made me desolate.
en.B: He dragged me off the road and tore me to pieces; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has left me devastated.
en.R: He dragged me off the path and tore me apart. \q He has left me ruined and alone.

pt.L: Os meus caminhos {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} desviou, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me despedaçou; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me deixou desolado.
pt.B: Ele me arrastou para fora da estrada e me fez em pedaços; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me deixou arrasado.
pt.R: Ele me arrastou para fora do caminho e me despedaçou. \q Ele me deixou arruinado e sozinho.

fr.L: Il a détourné mes chemins, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a déchiré ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a rendu désolé.
fr.B: Il m’a traîné hors de la route et m’a mis en pièces ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a laissé dévasté.
fr.R: Il m’a traîné hors du chemin et m’a déchiré. \q Il m’a laissé ruiné et seul.

es.L: Mis caminos ha desviado, y me ha despedazado; \q me ha dejado desolado.
es.B: Me arrastró fuera del camino y me hizo pedazos; \q me ha dejado devastado.
es.R: Me sacó a rastras del camino y me destrozó. \q Me ha dejado arruinado y solo.

vi.L: Các đường lối tôi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cho rẽ ngang, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã xé xác tôi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm tôi hoang tàn.
vi.B: Ngài lôi tôi ra khỏi đường và xé tôi ra từng mảnh; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã để tôi tan hoang.
vi.R: Ngài lôi tôi ra khỏi lối đi và xé nát tôi. \q Ngài để tôi tan nát và cô đơn.

sw.L: Njia zangu amezigeuza, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} amenirarua vipande vipande; \q amenifanya ukiwa.
sw.B: Aliniburuta kutoka njiani, akanirarua vipande vipande; \q ameniacha nimeharibika kabisa.
sw.R: Aliniburuta nje ya njia, akanirarua. \q Ameniacha nikiwa nimeharibika na peke yangu.

ko.L: 그분께서 내 길들을 벗어나게 하시고 나를 찢으셨다. \q 나를 황폐하게 하셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 나를 길에서 끌어내어 갈기갈기 찢으시고, \q 나를 폐허처럼 버려두셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 나를 길에서 끌어내어 찢으셨다. \q 나를 망가뜨려 홀로 남겨 두셨다.

decisions.choice: turned aside my ways: dragged me off the path
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn aside. Following verse 10, it pictures the beast dragging its prey off the road. It may also mean that God has turned the man's paths away, so that he goes astray.

decisions.choice: torn in pieces: a rare word
decisions.reason: The verb (pashach) is found only here in the Hebrew Bible. A related word in Aramaic means to tear or pull apart, which fits the picture of the bear and the lion.

decisions.choice: desolate: left ruined and stunned
decisions.reason: The word (shomem) is used of places laid waste and of people left stunned and alone (2 Samuel 13:20; Lamentations 1:4, 13, 16).

decisions.choice: dragged me off the road / path
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the picture of verse 10 (m1).

records.literal_gloss: He has bent his bow and set me up like the target for the arrow.

en.L: He has trodden {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} bow and set me up \q like the target for the arrow.
en.B: He has drawn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} bow \q and set me up as a target for arrows.
en.R: He has pulled back the string of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} bow \q and made me the target for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arrows.

pt.L: Ele pisou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} arco e me pôs \q como o alvo para a flecha.
pt.B: Ele armou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} arco \q e me pôs como alvo das flechas.
pt.R: Ele puxou a corda do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} arco \q e fez de mim o alvo das {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} flechas.

fr.L: Il a tendu {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} arc et m’a placé \q comme la cible pour la flèche.
fr.B: Il a bandé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} arc \q et m’a placé comme cible pour les flèches.
fr.R: Il a tiré la corde de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} arc \q et a fait de moi la cible de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} flèches.

es.L: Ha pisado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} arco y me ha puesto \q como blanco para la flecha.
es.B: Ha tensado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} arco \q y me ha puesto como blanco para las flechas.
es.R: Ha tirado de la cuerda de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} arco \q y me ha hecho el blanco de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} flechas.

vi.L: Ngài đã đạp cung của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và dựng tôi lên \q như cái đích cho mũi tên.
vi.B: Ngài đã giương cung \q và đặt tôi làm đích cho các mũi tên.
vi.R: Ngài đã kéo căng dây cung \q và lấy tôi làm đích cho các mũi tên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

sw.L: Ameukanyaga upinde {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na kunisimamisha \q kama shabaha ya mshale.
sw.B: Ameuvuta upinde {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} \q na kunifanya shabaha ya mishale.
sw.R: Ameivuta kamba ya upinde {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} \q na kunifanya shabaha ya mishale {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

ko.L: 그분께서 그분의 활을 밟아 메우시고 나를 세우셨다, \q 화살의 과녁처럼.
ko.B: 그분께서 활을 당기시고 \q 나를 화살의 과녁으로 삼으셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 활시위를 당기시고 \q 나를 그분의 화살 과녁으로 삼으셨다.

decisions.choice: trodden his bow: strung and readied his bow
decisions.reason: The verb (darakh) means to tread. A large bow was strung by bracing it with the foot, so 'treading the bow' means getting it ready to shoot (Psalm 7:13; Lamentations 2:4).

decisions.choice: a target: as Job complains
decisions.reason: Job says God has set him up as his target, and his archers surround him (Job 16:12-13; compare 7:20).

decisions.choice: his arrows
decisions.reason: Readable says 'his arrows'; the Hebrew has 'the arrow', the one God shoots.

records.literal_gloss: He has brought into my kidneys [the] sons of his quiver.

en.L: He has made enter into my kidneys \q the sons of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} quiver.
en.B: He has driven deep into my inner being \q the arrows from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} quiver.
en.R: He has shot {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} arrows \q deep inside me.

pt.L: Ele fez entrar nos meus rins \q os filhos da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} aljava.
pt.B: Ele cravou bem fundo no meu íntimo \q as flechas da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} aljava.
pt.R: Ele atirou as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} flechas \q bem dentro de mim.

fr.L: Il a fait entrer dans mes reins \q les fils de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} carquois.
fr.B: Il a enfoncé au plus profond de moi \q les flèches de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} carquois.
fr.R: Il a tiré {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} flèches \q au plus profond de moi.

es.L: Ha hecho entrar en mis riñones \q los hijos de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} aljaba.
es.B: Ha clavado en lo más hondo de mi ser \q las flechas de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} aljaba.
es.R: Me ha disparado {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} flechas \q hasta lo más hondo.

vi.L: Ngài đã khiến đi vào thận tôi \q những đứa con của ống tên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ngài đã bắn sâu vào tận tâm can tôi \q những mũi tên từ ống tên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ngài đã bắn các mũi tên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} \q vào sâu trong tôi.

sw.L: Ameingiza ndani ya figo zangu \q wana wa podo {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.B: Ameichoma ndani kabisa ya nafsi yangu \q mishale kutoka podo {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.R: Amepiga mishale {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} \q ndani yangu kabisa.

ko.L: 그분께서 내 콩팥에 들어가게 하셨다, \q 그분의 화살통의 아들들을.
ko.B: 그분께서 내 속 깊은 곳에 \q 화살통의 화살들을 꽂으셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 화살을 쏘셔서 \q 내 몸 깊숙이 박히게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: fifth letter: he (verses 13-15)
decisions.reason: Verses 13-15 each begin with he, the fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: the sons of his quiver: his arrows
decisions.reason: Hebrew can call something the 'son' of what holds or produces it. The 'sons of the quiver' are the arrows it holds.

decisions.choice: my kidneys: my inmost self
decisions.reason: The kidneys were thought of as the seat of the deepest feelings, hidden inside the body (Psalm 73:21; Jeremiah 12:2). The arrows strike to the heart of who he is, as in Job 16:13.

decisions.choice: inner being / deep inside me; arrows
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the two pictures mean (m2, m3); Literal keeps them.

records.literal_gloss: I have become a laughingstock to all my people, their taunt-song all the day.

en.L: I have become a laughingstock to all my people, \q their mocking song all the day.
en.B: I have become a joke to all my people, \q the song they mock me with all day long.
en.R: All my people laugh at me. \q All day long they sing songs that make fun of me.

pt.L: Tornei-me motivo de riso para todo o meu povo, \q a canção de zombaria deles o dia todo.
pt.B: Virei piada para todo o meu povo, \q a canção com que zombam de mim o dia inteiro.
pt.R: Todo o meu povo ri de mim. \q O dia inteiro eles cantam músicas para zombar de mim.

fr.L: Je suis devenu la risée de tout mon peuple, \q leur chanson moqueuse tout le jour.
fr.B: Je suis devenu la risée de tout mon peuple, \q leur refrain moqueur toute la journée.
fr.R: Tout mon peuple rit de moi. \q Toute la journée, ils chantent des chansons pour se moquer de moi.

es.L: He llegado a ser el hazmerreír de todo mi pueblo, \q su copla burlona todo el día.
es.B: Me he vuelto el hazmerreír de todo mi pueblo, \q la canción con que se burlan de mí todo el día.
es.R: Todo mi pueblo se ríe de mí. \q Todo el día cantan canciones para burlarse de mí.

vi.L: Tôi đã trở thành trò cười cho cả dân tôi, \q bài ca chế nhạo của họ suốt ngày.
vi.B: Tôi đã thành trò cười cho cả dân tôi, \q thành bài hát họ chế giễu tôi suốt ngày.
vi.R: Cả dân tôi đều cười nhạo tôi. \q Suốt ngày họ hát những bài chế giễu tôi.

sw.L: Nimekuwa kicheko kwa watu wangu wote, \q wimbo wao wa dhihaka mchana kutwa.
sw.B: Nimekuwa kichekesho kwa watu wangu wote, \q wimbo wanaonidhihaki nao mchana kutwa.
sw.R: Watu wangu wote wananicheka. \q Mchana kutwa wanaimba nyimbo za kunidhihaki.

ko.L: 내가 내 모든 백성에게 웃음거리가 되었고, \q 온종일 그들의 조롱하는 노래가 되었다.
ko.B: 나는 내 모든 백성의 놀림감이 되었고, \q 온종일 그들이 나를 조롱하는 노래가 되었다.
ko.R: 내 백성이 모두 나를 비웃는다. \q 온종일 나를 놀리는 노래를 부른다.

decisions.choice: my people: the reading of the standard Hebrew text
decisions.reason: Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac translation read 'all peoples', which would make the mockers foreign nations, as in verse 45. The standard text reads 'all my people': his own people laugh at him, as Jeremiah's did (Jeremiah 20:7).

decisions.choice: mocking song: a song made up to taunt someone
decisions.reason: The word (neginah) is a song played on strings. Here it is a song people sing about him to mock him, as in Job 30:9 and Psalm 69:13; it returns in verse 63.

records.literal_gloss: He has filled me with bitter [things]; he has made me drink [my] fill [of] wormwood.

en.L: He has filled me with bitter things; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made me drink my fill of wormwood.
en.B: He has fed me full of bitter things \q and made me drink wormwood until I could take no more.
en.R: He has given me only bitter things to eat. \q He has made me drink bitter wormwood.

pt.L: Ele me fartou de amarguras; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me fez beber até me saciar de absinto.
pt.B: Ele me encheu de coisas amargas \q e me fez beber absinto até eu não aguentar mais.
pt.R: Ele só me deu coisas amargas para comer. \q Ele me fez beber absinto amargo.

fr.L: Il m’a rassasié d’amertumes ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a abreuvé d’absinthe.
fr.B: Il m’a gavé de choses amères \q et m’a fait boire de l’absinthe jusqu’à n’en plus pouvoir.
fr.R: Il ne m’a donné que des choses amères à manger. \q Il m’a fait boire de l’absinthe amère.

es.L: Me ha llenado de amarguras; \q me ha hecho beber hasta saciarme de ajenjo.
es.B: Me ha hartado de amarguras \q y me ha hecho beber ajenjo hasta no poder más.
es.R: Solo me ha dado cosas amargas para comer. \q Me ha hecho beber ajenjo amargo.

vi.L: Ngài đã làm cho tôi đầy những điều cay đắng; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã cho tôi uống ngải đắng no nê.
vi.B: Ngài đã cho tôi ăn đầy những điều cay đắng \q và bắt tôi uống ngải đắng đến không chịu nổi.
vi.R: Ngài chỉ cho tôi ăn những thứ đắng. \q Ngài bắt tôi uống ngải đắng.

sw.L: Amenijaza vitu vichungu; \q amenishibisha pakanga.
sw.B: Amenilisha vitu vichungu mpaka nikashiba \q na kuninywesha pakanga hata nisiweze kustahimili.
sw.R: Amenipa vitu vichungu tu vya kula. \q Amenipa pakanga chungu ninywe.

ko.L: 그분께서 쓴 것들로 나를 배불리시고, \q 쓴 쑥을 실컷 마시게 하셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 쓴 것들로 내 배를 채우시고, \q 더는 견딜 수 없을 만큼 쓴 쑥을 마시게 하셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 나에게 쓴 것만 먹게 하셨다. \q 쓴 쑥을 마시게 하셨다.

decisions.choice: wormwood: a bitter plant, a picture of bitter suffering
decisions.reason: Wormwood (la'anah) is a plant with a very bitter taste. The prophets use it, with the poison of verse 5, for the bitterness of judgment (Jeremiah 9:14; 23:15; Amos 6:12). It returns in verse 19.

decisions.choice: filled ... made drink my fill: given more than he can bear
decisions.reason: Both verbs mean to be filled or sated, one with food and one with drink. He has had all the bitterness a person can take.

decisions.choice: to eat
decisions.reason: Readable says the bitter things are food, paired with the drink.

decisions.choice: absinto
decisions.reason: "Absinto" is the Portuguese name of the bitter plant (m1) and the word Portuguese readers know from the prophets and Revelation 8:11; "losna", the same plant's everyday name, is regional.

records.literal_gloss: And he has broken with gravel my teeth; he has made me cower in ash[es].

en.L: He has broken my teeth with gravel; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has pressed me down in the ashes.
en.B: He has made me break my teeth on gravel; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has trampled me down in the ashes.
en.R: He has made me break my teeth on stones. \q He has pushed me down into the ashes.

pt.L: Ele quebrou os meus dentes com cascalho; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me afundou na cinza.
pt.B: Ele me fez quebrar os dentes no cascalho; \q {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me pisoteou na cinza.
pt.R: Ele me fez quebrar os dentes em pedras. \q Ele me empurrou para dentro da cinza.

fr.L: Il a brisé mes dents avec du gravier ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a enfoncé dans la cendre.
fr.B: Il m’a fait briser les dents sur du gravier ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a piétiné dans la cendre.
fr.R: Il m’a fait casser les dents sur des cailloux. \q Il m’a poussé à terre dans la cendre.

es.L: Me ha quebrado los dientes con cascajo; \q me ha hundido en la ceniza.
es.B: Me ha hecho romperme los dientes con piedrecillas; \q me ha pisoteado en la ceniza.
es.R: Me ha hecho romperme los dientes con piedras. \q Me ha empujado hasta la ceniza.

vi.L: Ngài đã làm gãy răng tôi bằng sỏi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ấn tôi xuống trong tro bụi.
vi.B: Ngài bắt tôi nhai sỏi đến gãy răng; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã giày đạp tôi trong tro bụi.
vi.R: Ngài khiến tôi gãy răng vì nhai phải sỏi đá. \q Ngài đã đẩy tôi xuống đống tro.

sw.L: Amevunja meno yangu kwa changarawe; \q amenikandamiza katika majivu.
sw.B: Amenifanya nivunje meno yangu kwa changarawe; \q amenikanyaga katika majivu.
sw.R: Amenifanya nivunje meno yangu kwa mawe. \q Amenisukuma chini katika majivu.

ko.L: 그분께서 자갈로 내 이를 부러뜨리시고, \q 나를 재 속에 짓누르셨다.
ko.B: 그분께서 자갈을 씹어 내 이가 부러지게 하시고, \q 나를 잿더미 속에 짓밟으셨다.
ko.R: 그분께서 돌을 씹어 내 이가 부러지게 하셨다. \q 나를 잿더미 속으로 밀어 넣으셨다.

decisions.choice: sixth letter: waw (verses 16-18)
decisions.reason: Verses 16-18 each begin with waw, the sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: broken my teeth with gravel: grit in his bread
decisions.reason: The picture is of bread full of grit that breaks the teeth of the one who eats it (compare Proverbs 20:17). God has given him hard and painful things to chew.

decisions.choice: pressed me down: a word found only here
decisions.reason: The verb (kafash) appears nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible. Related words suggest pressing down or trampling, so that he cowers in the ashes. The ancient Greek translation reads 'he has fed me ashes', which would continue the eating picture.

decisions.choice: ashes: the place of mourning and humiliation
decisions.reason: Mourners sat in ashes or put them on their heads (Job 2:8; Jeremiah 6:26).

records.literal_gloss: And has been rejected from peace my soul; I have forgotten good.

en.L: My soul has been cast away from peace; \q I have forgotten good.
en.B: My soul has been cut off from peace; \q I have forgotten what good is.
en.R: I have no peace left at all. \q I have forgotten what it is like to be happy.

pt.L: A minha alma foi lançada longe da paz; \q esqueci o bem.
pt.B: A minha alma foi afastada da paz; \q esqueci o que é o bem.
pt.R: Não me resta paz nenhuma. \q Esqueci como é ser feliz.

fr.L: Mon âme a été rejetée loin de la paix ; \q j’ai oublié le bonheur.
fr.B: Mon âme a été privée de paix ; \q j’ai oublié ce qu’est le bonheur.
fr.R: Je n’ai plus aucune paix. \q J’ai oublié ce que c’est d’être heureux.

es.L: Mi alma ha sido alejada de la paz; \q he olvidado el bien.
es.B: Mi alma ha quedado privada de la paz; \q he olvidado lo que es el bien.
es.R: Ya no me queda nada de paz. \q He olvidado lo que es ser feliz.

vi.L: Linh hồn tôi đã bị ném khỏi sự bình an; \q tôi đã quên điều tốt lành.
vi.B: Linh hồn tôi đã bị cắt lìa khỏi bình an; \q tôi đã quên mất hạnh phúc là gì.
vi.R: Tôi chẳng còn chút bình an nào. \q Tôi đã quên vui sướng là thế nào.

sw.L: Nafsi yangu imetupwa mbali na amani; \q nimesahau mema.
sw.B: Nafsi yangu imetengwa mbali na amani; \q nimesahau mema ni nini.
sw.R: Sina amani hata kidogo. \q Nimesahau jinsi ilivyo kuwa na furaha.

ko.L: 내 영혼이 평안에서 버림을 받았고, \q 나는 좋은 것을 잊어버렸다.
ko.B: 내 영혼은 평안을 빼앗겼고, \q 나는 행복이 무엇인지 잊어버렸다.
ko.R: 나에게는 평안이 하나도 남지 않았다. \q 행복하다는 것이 어떤 것인지 다 잊어버렸다.

decisions.choice: has been cast away: the soul as the one rejected
alternatives: you have rejected my soul from peace
decisions.reason: The verb form can be read 'it has been rejected' with 'my soul' as its subject, or 'you have rejected', speaking to God: 'you have rejected my soul from peace.' The ancient Greek reads 'he has rejected'. In each case God has put peace out of his reach.

decisions.choice: peace: wholeness and well-being
decisions.reason: Peace (shalom) is more than the absence of war: it is a life that is whole and well. 'Good' in the second line is the same thing seen as happiness and prosperity.

decisions.choice: my soul: my whole self
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) means the living person, the self with its desires and feelings, not a part of him that is separate from the body.

decisions.choice: I have no peace; to be happy
decisions.reason: Readable says 'I' for 'my soul' (m3) and says what 'good' means here (m2).

records.literal_gloss: And I said: Has perished my endurance and my hope from Yahweh.

en.L: And I said, "My lasting strength has perished, \q and my hope from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: So I said, "My strength is gone, \q and so is all I hoped for from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: So I said, "I cannot go on. \q I no longer hope that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will help me."

pt.L: E eu disse: "Pereceu a minha força duradoura, \q e a minha esperança {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}."
pt.B: Então eu disse: "A minha força acabou, \q e também tudo o que eu esperava {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}."
pt.R: Então eu disse: "Não consigo continuar. \q Já não espero que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me ajude."

fr.L: Et j’ai dit : « Ma force durable a péri, \q et mon espérance [venant] {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.B: Alors j’ai dit : « Ma force s’en est allée, \q et tout ce que j’espérais {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} aussi. »
fr.R: Alors j’ai dit : « Je ne peux plus continuer. \q Je n’espère plus que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’aidera. »

es.L: Y dije: «Ha perecido mi fuerza duradera, \q y mi esperanza [que venía] {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.B: Por eso dije: «Se me acabaron las fuerzas, \q y también todo lo que esperaba {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.R: Por eso dije: «Ya no puedo seguir. \q Ya no espero que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ayude».

vi.L: Và tôi nói: "Sức bền của tôi đã tiêu mất, \q và niềm hy vọng của tôi nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [cũng vậy]."
vi.B: Nên tôi nói: "Sức lực tôi đã tiêu tan, \q và mọi điều tôi trông mong nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cũng không còn."
vi.R: Nên tôi nói: "Tôi không thể chịu nổi nữa. \q Tôi không còn hy vọng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ giúp tôi."

sw.L: Nami nikasema, "Nguvu yangu ya kudumu imepotea, \q na tumaini langu kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.B: Basi nikasema, "Nguvu zangu zimekwisha, \q pamoja na yote niliyotumaini kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Basi nikasema, "Siwezi kuendelea. \q Situmaini tena kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atanisaidia."

ko.L: 그래서 내가 말하였다. "내 오랜 힘이 사라졌다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 [바라던] 내 소망도 [사라졌다]."
ko.B: 그래서 나는 말했다. "내 기력이 다했다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 바라던 것도 모두 사라졌다."
ko.R: 그래서 나는 말했다. "나는 더는 견딜 수 없다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나를 도와주시리라는 희망도 이제 없다."

decisions.choice: my lasting strength: endurance
decisions.reason: The word (netsach) means what lasts: endurance, lasting strength, sometimes splendor. He has no strength left to go on.

decisions.choice: my hope from the LORD: what he hoped to receive from the LORD
decisions.reason: The hope he has lost is the help he expected from the LORD. Here the LORD is named for the first time in the chapter; he is the 'he' of verses 1-16.

decisions.choice: I said: his thought, quoted
decisions.reason: He quotes what he said to himself in his despair. Verse 21 turns it around.

decisions.choice: I cannot go on; I no longer hope that the LORD will help me
decisions.reason: Readable says what lost endurance and lost hope mean here (m1, m2).

records.literal_gloss: Remember my affliction and my homelessness, wormwood and poison.

en.L: Remember my affliction and my homelessness, \q the wormwood and the poison.
en.B: Remember how I am afflicted and homeless, \q the wormwood and the bitter poison.
en.R: Remember how I suffer and have no home, \q how bitter it is, like poison.

pt.L: Lembra-te da minha aflição e da minha errância, \q do absinto e do veneno.
pt.B: Lembra-te de como estou aflito e sem lar, \q do absinto e do veneno amargo.
pt.R: Lembra-te de como eu sofro e não tenho casa, \q como isso é amargo, como veneno.

fr.L: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de mon affliction et de mon errance, \q de l’absinthe et du poison.
fr.B: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de ma misère et de mon errance, \q de l’absinthe et du poison amer.
fr.R: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de ma souffrance, de ma vie sans maison, \q de cette amertume qui est comme du poison.

es.L: Acuérdate de mi aflicción y de mi andar errante, \q del ajenjo y del veneno.
es.B: Acuérdate de mi miseria y de mi vida sin hogar, \q del ajenjo y del veneno amargo.
es.R: Acuérdate de cómo sufro y de que no tengo hogar, \q de lo amargo que es, como veneno.

vi.L: Xin nhớ đến sự khốn khổ và cảnh lưu lạc của tôi, \q ngải đắng và chất độc.
vi.B: Xin nhớ đến nỗi khốn khổ và cảnh không nhà của tôi, \q ngải đắng và chất độc đắng cay.
vi.R: Xin nhớ tôi đau khổ và không nhà thế nào, \q cay đắng như thuốc độc.

sw.L: Kumbuka mateso yangu na kutangatanga kwangu, \q pakanga na sumu.
sw.B: Kumbuka jinsi ninavyoteseka na kukosa makao, \q pakanga na sumu chungu.
sw.R: Kumbuka jinsi ninavyoteseka na kukosa makao, \q jinsi ilivyo chungu kama sumu.

ko.L: 제 고난과 떠돌아다님을, \q 쓴 쑥과 독을 기억하여 주십시오.
ko.B: 제가 고난을 당하고 집 없이 떠도는 것을, \q 쓴 쑥과 쓰디쓴 독 같은 이 일을 기억해 주십시오.
ko.R: 제가 얼마나 고통당하고 집도 없이 떠도는지 기억해 주십시오. \q 그것은 독처럼 쓰디씁니다.

decisions.choice: seventh letter: zayin (verses 19-21)
decisions.reason: Verses 19-21 each begin with zayin, the seventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: remember: a plea to God
alternatives: the memory of my affliction is wormwood and poison
decisions.reason: The verb is a command, and the one asked to remember is God, to whom the man speaks for the first time. It could also be read as a noun, 'the remembering of my affliction ... is wormwood and poison', which would lead straight into verse 20.

decisions.choice: my affliction and my homelessness: Zion's words in 1:7
decisions.reason: The same pair of words describes Jerusalem in 1:7, remembering her days of affliction and wandering. The man's lament and the city's are one. 'Homelessness' (marud) is the life of someone driven from home (Isaiah 58:7).

decisions.choice: wormwood and poison: bitter suffering, as in verses 5 and 15
decisions.reason: The two bitter plants return from verses 5 and 15.

decisions.choice: how bitter it is, like poison
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two bitter plants stand for.

decisions.choice: Lembra-te (tu)
decisions.reason: The man speaks to God for the first time (m2), and like Zion in chapters 1-2 he says "tu": "Lembra-te". Literal repeats "errância" from 1:7, where the same pair of words describes Jerusalem (m3).

decisions.choice: "mon affliction et mon errance" (L), "ma misère et mon errance" (B), the words of 1:7
decisions.reason: The man takes up Zion’s words of 1:7 (m3), so Literal and Balanced repeat that verse’s French nouns.

decisions.choice: "aflicción y ... andar errante" (L); "miseria y ... vida sin hogar" (B)
decisions.reason: The two nouns are the ones Zion used of herself in 1:7, so each level repeats its own wording from there.

decisions.choice: "기억하여 주십시오": a short plea to God in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: The imperative is addressed to God, as the meaning decision says, so Korean must use the prayer style here; 3:20-21 return to the plain style of the man's own thoughts.

records.literal_gloss: Surely remembers and is bowed down upon me my soul.

en.L: My soul indeed remembers \q and sinks down within me.
en.B: My soul keeps remembering it \q and is bowed low within me.
en.R: I think about it all the time, \q and I feel so low.

pt.L: A minha alma certamente se lembra \q e se abate dentro de mim.
pt.B: A minha alma não para de se lembrar disso \q e se curva dentro de mim.
pt.R: Eu penso nisso o tempo todo, \q e me sinto muito abatido.

fr.L: Mon âme s’en souvient sans cesse \q et s’affaisse en moi.
fr.B: Mon âme ne cesse de s’en souvenir \q et elle est abattue au-dedans de moi.
fr.R: J’y pense tout le temps, \q et je me sens si abattu.

es.L: Ciertamente mi alma [lo] recuerda \q y se abate dentro de mí.
es.B: Mi alma no deja de recordarlo \q y está abatida dentro de mí.
es.R: Lo pienso todo el tiempo, \q y me siento hundido.

vi.L: Linh hồn tôi hẳn nhớ mãi \q và chùng xuống trong tôi.
vi.B: Linh hồn tôi cứ nhớ mãi điều ấy \q và sầu não trong tôi.
vi.R: Tôi cứ nghĩ về điều ấy mãi, \q và tôi thấy lòng mình chùng xuống.

sw.L: Hakika nafsi yangu inakumbuka \q na kuinama ndani yangu.
sw.B: Nafsi yangu inaendelea kuyakumbuka \q na imeinama chini ndani yangu.
sw.R: Ninayafikiria wakati wote, \q nami ninavunjika moyo sana.

ko.L: 내 영혼이 정녕 기억하고 \q 내 속에서 가라앉는다.
ko.B: 내 영혼은 그것을 자꾸만 떠올리며 \q 내 속에서 낮아진다.
ko.R: 나는 늘 그 일을 생각한다. \q 그래서 마음이 몹시 무겁다.

decisions.choice: my soul surely remembers: the soul is the subject
decisions.reason: The doubled verb stresses the remembering. Its form could also be 'you will surely remember', addressed to God after the plea of verse 19: 'you will surely remember, and my soul is bowed down within me.'

decisions.choice: is bowed down: the reading marked in the margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read 'it broods' or 'it complains' (tashiach, compare Psalm 77:4); the reading marked in the margin, which this translation follows, is 'it is bowed down' (tashoach, as in Psalm 42:6). An old Jewish list of scribal changes also holds that the verse once read 'your soul', meaning God's: 'your soul will remember and bend down to me.'

decisions.choice: I feel so low
decisions.reason: Readable says 'I' for 'my soul' and gives the sense of being bowed down.

records.literal_gloss: This I bring back to my heart; therefore I will hope.

en.L: This I bring back to my heart; \q therefore I will hope:
en.B: Yet I bring this back to mind, \q and because of it I will wait in hope:
en.R: But then I think of something else, \q and it gives me hope:

pt.L: Isto eu trago de volta ao meu coração; \q por isso esperarei:
pt.B: Mas volto a pensar nisto, \q e por isso continuo esperando:
pt.R: Mas então penso em outra coisa, \q e isso me dá esperança:

fr.L: Ceci, je le ramène à mon cœur ; \q c’est pourquoi j’espérerai :
fr.B: Pourtant, voici ce que je me remets en mémoire, \q et à cause de cela j’attendrai avec espérance :
fr.R: Mais ensuite je pense à autre chose, \q et cela me donne de l’espoir :

es.L: Esto traigo de nuevo a mi corazón; \q por eso esperaré:
es.B: Pero esto vuelvo a traer a la memoria, \q y por eso mantendré la esperanza:
es.R: Pero luego pienso en otra cosa, \q y eso me da esperanza:

vi.L: Điều này tôi đem trở lại trong lòng; \q vì thế tôi sẽ hy vọng:
vi.B: Nhưng tôi nhớ lại điều này, \q và nhờ đó tôi sẽ chờ đợi trong hy vọng:
vi.R: Nhưng rồi tôi nghĩ đến một điều khác, \q và điều ấy cho tôi hy vọng:

sw.L: Hili ninalirudisha moyoni mwangu; \q kwa hiyo nitatumaini:
sw.B: Lakini ninalikumbuka jambo hili, \q na kwa sababu yake nitangoja kwa tumaini:
sw.R: Lakini kisha ninafikiri jambo jingine, \q nalo linanipa tumaini:

ko.L: 이것을 내가 내 마음에 되돌린다. \q 그러므로 내가 소망을 품는다.
ko.B: 그러나 나는 이것을 다시 마음에 떠올린다. \q 그래서 나는 희망을 품고 기다린다.
ko.R: 그러나 나는 다른 것을 생각한다. \q 그것이 나에게 희망을 준다.

decisions.choice: this: what follows in verses 22-24
decisions.reason: 'This' points forward to what he calls to mind in verses 22-24, the LORD's loyal love and mercy. It could point back to his remembering in verse 20, so that the memory of suffering itself drives him to hope; but the turn of the poem comes with verse 22.

decisions.choice: bring back to my heart: call to mind
decisions.reason: The heart is the mind and will. To bring something back to it is to remember it on purpose and let it shape one's thinking (Deuteronomy 4:39; Isaiah 46:8).

decisions.choice: hope: wait with expectation
decisions.reason: The verb (yachal) means to wait for something with hope, as in verses 24 and 26 and Psalm 130:5. It is the reverse of the lost hope of verse 18.

decisions.choice: Yet / But
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the turn from despair to hope; the Hebrew shows it by what follows.

source.text: חַֽסְדֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ כִּ֣י לֹא־תָ֔מְנוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־כָל֖וּ רַחֲמָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] loyal loves of Yahweh: that not we are finished, for not have ended his compassions.

en.L: [It is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s loyal love that we are not consumed, \q for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercies have not come to an end.
en.B: It is by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s loyal love that we have not been wiped out, \q for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mercies have not failed.
en.R: We are still alive because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s faithful love. \q His mercies never run out.

pt.L: [É pelos atos de] amor leal {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} que não chegamos ao fim, \q pois as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} misericórdias não se acabaram.
pt.B: Por causa do amor leal {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} não fomos exterminados, \q pois as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} misericórdias não falharam.
pt.R: Ainda estamos vivos por causa do amor fiel {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. \q As {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} misericórdias nunca se esgotam.

fr.L: [C’est grâce à] l’amour loyal {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} que nous ne sommes pas consumés, \q car {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} compassions n’ont pas pris fin.
fr.B: C’est par l’amour fidèle {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} que nous n’avons pas été anéantis, \q car {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} compassions ne se sont pas taries.
fr.R: Nous sommes encore en vie grâce à l’amour fidèle {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Sa tendresse ne s’épuise jamais.

es.L: [Es por] el amor leal {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que no hemos perecido, \q porque no se han agotado {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} compasiones.
es.B: Gracias al amor fiel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} no hemos sido aniquilados, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} compasión no se ha acabado.
es.R: Seguimos vivos por el amor fiel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q Su compasión nunca se acaba.

vi.L: [Bởi] tình yêu thương thành tín của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nên chúng ta không bị tiêu diệt, \q vì những lòng thương xót của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chưa đến hồi chấm dứt.
vi.B: Nhờ tình yêu thương thành tín của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà chúng ta không bị xóa sạch, \q vì lòng thương xót của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng hề vơi cạn.
vi.R: Chúng ta vẫn còn sống là nhờ tình thương không hề thay đổi của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Lòng thương xót của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không bao giờ cạn.

sw.L: [Ni] upendo usiokoma wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwamba hatujamalizwa, \q kwa maana huruma {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} hazijafikia mwisho.
sw.B: Ni kwa upendo usiokoma wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwamba hatujafutiliwa mbali, \q kwa maana huruma {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} hazijapungua.
sw.R: Bado tuko hai kwa sababu ya upendo usiokoma wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Huruma {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} haziishi kamwe.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 한결같은 사랑으로 우리가 소멸되지 않았다. \q 그분의 긍휼이 그치지 않았기 때문이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 한결같은 사랑 덕분에 우리가 멸망하지 않았다. \q 그분의 긍휼이 다함이 없기 때문이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 변함없는 사랑 때문에 우리가 아직 살아 있다. \q 그분의 자비는 결코 바닥나지 않는다.

decisions.choice: eighth letter: heth (verses 22-24)
decisions.reason: Verses 22-24 each begin with heth, the eighth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: we are not consumed: the reading of the standard Hebrew text
alternatives: the LORD's loyal love has not ceased
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads 'we are not finished' (tamnu): it is because of the LORD's loyal love that the people have not been wiped out. The Aramaic Targum and the Syriac translation, followed by many modern readers, have 'they have not ceased' (tammu, one letter different): 'the LORD's loyal love does not cease, his mercies do not come to an end.' That reading matches the second line closely; the standard text is followed here.

decisions.choice: loyal love: the LORD's faithful, covenant kindness, here in the plural
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that keeps faith, the kindness of someone bound to another by a promise (Exodus 34:6). It is plural here, the LORD's many acts of loyal love, as in Isaiah 63:7 and Psalm 89:2.

decisions.choice: mercies: tender compassion, kept distinct from loyal love
decisions.reason: The word (rachamim) is related to the word for the womb, the deep feeling of a parent for a child (Isaiah 49:15). It is a different word from loyal love in the first line, and the two together say why the people still live.

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, chesed is 'loyal love' at Literal and Balanced and 'faithful love' at Readable, and rachamim is 'mercies' at every level.

decisions.choice: We are still alive because of
decisions.reason: Readable puts the people first and says positively what 'not consumed' means.

decisions.choice: amor leal (L, B); amor fiel (R); misericórdias (every level); [os atos de] (L)
decisions.reason: As in the Psalms and Isaiah, chesed is "amor leal" at Literal and Balanced and "amor fiel" at Readable, and rachamim is "misericórdias", a different word, at every level (m3, m4). The plural chesed is "[os atos de] amor leal" at Literal, as in Psalm 89:2. Verses 22-26 are well known in Portuguese, so they are drafted from the Hebrew and the gloss; only short common phrases are shared with familiar versions.

decisions.choice: "l’amour loyal" (L), "l’amour fidèle" (B, R) for ḥesed; "compassions" (L, B), "tendresse" (R) for raḥamim
decisions.reason: As published Isaiah and the Psalms for ḥesed; raḥamim keeps its own word, apart from "amour" (m4), and the verb of verse 32 takes the same family ("compassion", "tendresse"). Drafted from the gloss, away from the familiar French wording of these verses.

decisions.choice: "amor leal" (L), "amor fiel" (B, R); "compasiones" (L), "compasión" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Hesed is worded as everywhere in the Spanish Old Testament. The second word (rahamim) is kept apart from it with "compasión", so the two do not merge into the one "misericordia" familiar from older Spanish versions; the verses were drafted from the Hebrew and kept away from that familiar wording.

decisions.choice: "tình yêu thương thành tín" (Literal, Balanced) and "tình thương không hề thay đổi" (Readable) for "hesed"; "lòng thương xót" for "rachamim"
decisions.reason: Hesed is the prophets' "tình yêu thương thành tín"; "lòng thương xót" is kept for the other word, tender compassion, so the two stay apart as the meaning decisions ask (also 3:32). Verses 22–23 were worded from the Hebrew and the gloss, not from a familiar version.

decisions.choice: "upendo usiokoma" for hesed; "huruma" for rachamim
decisions.reason: Hesed is "upendo usiokoma" at every level, as in Isaiah, Jeremiah and the Psalms (also in verse 32), and rachamim, the LORD's tender mercies, is kept distinct as "huruma". Verses 22-26 were drafted from the Hebrew and the gloss and worded apart from the familiar Swahili versions of these lines.

decisions.choice: "한결같은 사랑" (Literal, Balanced) / "변함없는 사랑" (Readable) for hesed; "긍휼" (Literal, Balanced) / "자비" (Readable) for the mercies
decisions.reason: Hesed keeps the word used for it through the Korean Old Testament, and the mercies (rachamim) keep a different word, so the two stay distinct as the meaning decision asks. These lines were drafted from the gloss; they do not reuse the familiar wording of the older Korean Bibles.

records.literal_gloss: [They are] new to the mornings; great [is] your faithfulness.

en.L: [They are] new morning by morning; \q great [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness.
en.B: They are new each morning; \q how great is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness!
en.R: They are new every morning. \q How faithful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are!

pt.L: [São] novas a cada manhã; \q grande [é] a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} fidelidade.
pt.B: Renovam-se cada manhã; \q como é grande a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} fidelidade!
pt.R: Elas são novas todas as manhãs. \q Como {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és fiel!

fr.L: [Elles sont] nouvelles matin après matin ; \q grande [est] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} fidélité.
fr.B: Elles sont nouvelles chaque matin ; \q que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} fidélité est grande !
fr.R: Elle est neuve chaque matin. \q Comme {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es fidèle !

es.L: [Son] nuevas mañana tras mañana; \q grande [es] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fidelidad.
es.B: Cada mañana vuelven a ser nuevas; \q ¡qué grande es {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fidelidad!
es.R: Cada mañana se renuevan. \q ¡Qué fiel eres!

vi.L: [Chúng] mới mỗi buổi sáng; \q lớn thay sự thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Mỗi buổi sáng chúng lại mới; \q sự thành tín của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật lớn lao!
vi.R: Mỗi buổi sáng chúng đều mới mẻ. \q Ngài thật thành tín biết bao!

sw.L: [Ni] mpya asubuhi kwa asubuhi; \q mkuu [ni] uaminifu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Zinafanywa upya kila asubuhi; \q jinsi ulivyo mkuu uaminifu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}!
sw.R: Kila asubuhi zinaanza upya. \q Jinsi {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ulivyo mwaminifu!

ko.L: [그것들이] 아침마다 새롭습니다. \q 주님의 신실하심이 크십니다.
ko.B: 그것은 아침마다 새롭습니다. \q 주님의 신실하심은 얼마나 크신지요!
ko.R: 그것은 아침마다 새롭습니다. \q 주님은 참으로 신실하십니다!

decisions.choice: they are new: the LORD's mercies and loyal love
decisions.reason: 'New' is plural and has no stated subject. It refers to the loyal love and mercies of verse 22: each morning brings them fresh.

decisions.choice: your faithfulness: the man now speaks to God
decisions.reason: In the middle of the confession the man turns from speaking about the LORD to speaking to him.

decisions.choice: faithfulness: firmness, reliability
decisions.reason: The word ('emunah) is from the same root as 'amen'. It means being firm and trustworthy, keeping one's word (Deuteronomy 32:4; Psalm 36:6).

decisions.choice: every morning: the time of rescue
decisions.reason: Morning was the time when help came after a night of danger (Psalm 30:6; 46:6; Isaiah 33:2).

decisions.choice: a tua fidelidade (tu)
decisions.reason: The man turns from speaking about the LORD to speaking to him (m2), so Portuguese uses "tu" at every level, as the Hebrew "your" requires; "a sua fidelidade" would lose the turn to prayer.

decisions.choice: "Elle est neuve", singular
decisions.reason: At Readable the subject is "sa tendresse" of verse 22, a singular noun in French, so the pronoun is singular; Literal and Balanced keep the plural of "compassions".

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun on "tu"; none on "eres"
decisions.reason: The man now speaks to God. Literal and Balanced have a free pronoun ("tu") and take the span; Readable says it with the verb alone ("¡Qué fiel eres!"), where Spanish has no separate pronoun to capitalize.

decisions.choice: the man now speaks to God in 합쇼체: "주님의 신실하심이 크십니다"
decisions.reason: "Your faithfulness" turns the confession into prayer, so Korean moves to the formal polite style for this verse; 3:24 goes back to speaking about the LORD. "신실하심" is the word the Korean Psalms use for God's faithfulness.

source.text: חֶלְקִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אָמְרָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י עַל־כֵּ֖ן אוֹחִ֥יל לֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: My portion [is] Yahweh, says my soul; therefore I will hope in him.

en.L: "My portion [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," says my soul; \q "therefore I will wait in hope for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is my portion," I tell myself, \q "and so I will wait for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in hope."
en.R: I say to myself, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is all I have. \q So I will put my hope in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

pt.L: "A minha porção [é] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}", diz a minha alma; \q "por isso aguardarei por {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} com esperança."
pt.B: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é a parte que me cabe", digo a mim mesmo, \q "e por isso vou esperar por {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} confiante."
pt.R: Digo a mim mesmo: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é tudo o que eu tenho. \q Por isso vou pôr a minha esperança {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}."

fr.L: « Ma part [est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} », dit mon âme ; \q « c’est pourquoi j’espérerai en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »
fr.B: « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est ma part », me dis-je, \q « aussi je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}attendrai avec espérance. »
fr.R: Je me dis : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est tout ce que j’ai. \q Alors je mets mon espoir en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »

es.L: «Mi porción [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}», dice mi alma; \q «por eso esperaré en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».
es.B: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es mi porción», me digo a mí mismo, \q «y por eso pondré en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mi esperanza».
es.R: Me digo a mí mismo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es todo lo que tengo. \q Por eso pongo en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mi esperanza».

vi.L: "Phần của tôi [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}," linh hồn tôi nói; \q "vì thế tôi sẽ trông đợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.B: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là phần của tôi," tôi tự nhủ, \q "nên tôi sẽ trông đợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong hy vọng."
vi.R: Tôi tự nhủ: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} là tất cả những gì tôi có. \q Vì thế tôi sẽ đặt hy vọng nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."

sw.L: "Fungu langu [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}," yasema nafsi yangu; \q "kwa hiyo nitamngoja kwa tumaini."
sw.B: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ndiye sehemu yangu," ninajiambia, \q "kwa hiyo nitamngoja kwa tumaini."
sw.R: Ninajiambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ndiye kila kitu nilicho nacho. \q Kwa hiyo nitaweka tumaini langu {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}."

ko.L: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 나의 몫이시다" 하고 내 영혼이 말한다. \q "그러므로 내가 그분을 바라고 기다리겠다."
ko.B: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 나의 몫이시다." 나는 스스로에게 말한다. \q "그러므로 나는 그분을 바라며 기다리겠다."
ko.R: 나는 혼잣말을 한다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 내가 가진 전부이시다. \q 그러니 나는 그분께 희망을 두겠다."

decisions.choice: my portion is the LORD: the Levites' share, and the psalmists' confession
decisions.reason: The Levites received no share of the land, because the LORD himself was their portion (Numbers 18:20; Deuteronomy 10:9). The psalmists use the same words for having God when everything else is gone (Psalm 16:5; 73:26; 142:6). The man has lost everything but has not lost the LORD.

decisions.choice: portion: a share of land or goods, an inheritance
decisions.reason: The word (cheleq) is a share given out to someone, especially a share of the land.

decisions.choice: says my soul: he says it to himself, with his whole being
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, the soul is the whole self. He speaks the words over himself.

decisions.choice: I tell myself / I say to myself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'I tell myself' for 'says my soul' (m3).

decisions.choice: all I have
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for the LORD to be one's portion (m1).

decisions.choice: a parte que me cabe
decisions.reason: The portion is the Levites' share of the land (m1, m2). Literal keeps "porção"; Balanced says "a parte que me cabe", plain Portuguese for a share given to someone, where "herança" would point to inheritance alone.

decisions.choice: "mi porción"
decisions.reason: "Porción" keeps the picture of a share of land, the Levites' share that was the LORD himself, as the Spanish Psalms word it; Readable says what it means.

records.literal_gloss: Good [is] Yahweh to [those] waiting for him, to [the] soul [that] seeks him.

en.L: Good [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to those who wait for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q to the soul that seeks {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good to all who wait in hope for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q to anyone who seeks {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is good to everyone who waits for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to act, \q to all who come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for help.

pt.L: Bom [é] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} com os que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} aguardam, \q com a alma que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} procura.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é bom para quem aguarda por {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} com esperança, \q para todo aquele que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} procura.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é bom com todos os que esperam que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} aja, \q com todos os que vêm a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pedir ajuda.

fr.L: Bon [est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}attendent, \q pour l’âme qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} cherche.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est bon pour tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}attendent avec espérance, \q pour quiconque {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} cherche.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est bon pour tous ceux qui attendent qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} agisse, \q pour tous ceux qui viennent {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander de l’aide.

es.L: Bueno [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} con los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} esperan, \q con el alma que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} busca.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es bueno con todos los que esperan en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q con todo el que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} busca.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es bueno con todos los que esperan a que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} actúe, \q con todos los que acuden a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pidiendo ayuda.

vi.L: Tốt lành [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đối với những người trông đợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q đối với linh hồn tìm kiếm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tốt lành với mọi người trông đợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong hy vọng, \q với bất cứ ai tìm kiếm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tốt lành với mọi người chờ đợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hành động, \q với tất cả những ai đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để xin giúp đỡ.

sw.L: Mwema [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa wale wanaomngoja, \q kwa nafsi inayomtafuta.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mwema kwa wote wanaomngoja kwa matumaini, \q kwa kila anayemtafuta.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni mwema kwa kila mtu anayemngoja atende, \q kwa wote wanaomjia kuomba msaada.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그분을 기다리는 자들에게, \q 그분을 찾는 영혼에게 선하시다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 희망을 품고 그분을 기다리는 모든 사람에게, \q 그분을 찾는 사람에게 선하시다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그분께서 일하시기를 기다리는 모든 사람에게, \q 도움을 구하러 그분께 나아오는 모든 사람에게 좋으신 분이다.

decisions.choice: ninth letter: teth (verses 25-27)
decisions.reason: Verses 25-27 each begin with teth, the ninth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see verse 1). All three begin with the word 'good' (tov).

decisions.choice: wait for him: look to him with hope
decisions.reason: The verb (qavah) means to wait with eager expectation, trusting that help will come (Psalm 27:14; Isaiah 40:31).

decisions.choice: seeks him: turns to him in prayer
decisions.reason: To seek the LORD (darash) is to turn to him, ask for his help and want to know his will (Deuteronomy 4:29; Psalm 34:11).

decisions.choice: the soul: the person
